justification: Inspected `byte-buddy-dep/src/main/java/net/bytebuddy/implementation/auxiliary/TypeProxy.java` and `byte-buddy-dep/src/test/java/net/bytebuddy/implementation/auxiliary/TypeProxyCreationTest.java`. `AccessorMethodInvocation` is a very small nested class (lines 667-711) with only two fields, one constructor, and two methods (`isValid`, `apply`), and it implements one cohesive task: registering an accessor and emitting a single bytecode compound. The surrounding `MethodCall`/`Appender` nesting already separates the broader proxy-building responsibilities, so there is no concrete evidence of insufficient modularization.
